steps.title: Signs: positive or negative?
steps.intro: Multiplication and division share the same sign rules. Addition has its own rules.

tables.title: Add
head: Signs
Result
rows: the sign of the number that is bigger in size: \(-7+3=-4\)

tips: Count only the minus signs: odd count → negative, even count → positive.
Even powers and \(|x|\) are never negative. Odd powers keep the sign: \((-2)^3=-8\).
Bigger minus smaller is positive, even for negative numbers: \(-2-(-5)=3\).
\(-x\) means "the opposite of \(x\)", not "a negative number".
Zero is neither positive nor negative.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} y\ne0 \\ \frac{x^6\cdot y^5}{|y|}<0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: \(x^6\) is an even power, so \(x^6\ge0\). If \(x=0\), the expression equals \(0\), which is not negative. Therefore \(x\ne0\) and \(x^6>0\).
The only piece that can make the expression negative is \(y^5\). An odd power keeps the sign, so \(y^5<0\) means \(y<0\).
Nothing is known about the sign of \(x\). Choice (1) claims too much (\(x<0\) is not necessarily true). Choices (2) and (4) say \(y>0\), which contradicts \(y<0\). The answer is (3).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} x<0<y \\ x+y>0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
explanation: x is negative and y is positive: mixed signs. In a sum with mixed signs, the number that is bigger in size wins.
The sum is positive, so the positive number y is bigger in size: \(|y|>|x|\).
The others: (1) is the opposite. (3) Mixed signs give a negative product: \(xy<0\). (4) \(x-y\) is smaller minus bigger, so it is negative.

steps.title: Consecutive integers
steps.intro: Write them with one letter, plug in the smallest legal numbers, or read the differences.
tips: Smaller minus bigger is negative: \(b-a=1\) but \(a-b=-1\).
"Greater than 0" does not mean the list starts at 1.
Plugging in? First check that the choices give different values. If two choices tie, choose other numbers.

steps.stem:
a, b and c are consecutive even numbers, and \(0<a<b<c\)
\(\frac{c^2-a^2}{b}=?\)
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(a=b-2\) and \(c=b+2\).

steps.stem:
a, b, c and d are consecutive integers, and \(a<b<c<d\)
\(\frac{d-a}{c-b}-\frac{a-c}{d-c}=?\)
explanation: In consecutive integers every difference is a fixed number: \(d-a=3\), \(c-b=1\), \(a-c=-2\), \(d-c=1\).
Watch the signs: \(a-c\) is smaller minus bigger, so it is negative. Subtracting a negative adds.

steps.stem: The sum of seven consecutive integers is \(91\). What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = count × middle, so the middle number is \(\frac{91}{7}=13\).
Seven numbers: three below the middle and three above it: \(10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16\).
The largest is \(13+3=16\). Check: \(7\cdot13=91\) ✓.

steps.stem: The sum of four consecutive integers is always —
explanation: Write the numbers as \(a, a+1, a+2, a+3\). The sum is \(4a+6\).
\(4a+6=2(2a+3)\), so the sum is always even.
\(4a+6=4(a+1)+2\): a multiple of 4, plus 2. So it is never divisible by 4.
Check: \(1+2+3+4=10\) and \(2+3+4+5=14\). Both are even and not divisible by 4. And \(10\) is not divisible by 3, so (4) is out.

steps.title: Sums of consecutive integers
steps.intro: Sum = count × middle. The middle = sum ÷ count.

head: Situation
Rule
Example
rows: the sum is divisible by the count
the sum is never divisible by the count

tips: Four consecutive integers: the sum is \(4a+6\), even but never divisible by 4.

steps.title: Even & odd
steps.intro: Plug in 2 for even and 1 or 3 for odd. For \(\pm\) and \(\times\), one plug-in for each parity case is enough. For division, plug in three times.
tips: In a sum, only the odd terms matter: an odd number of them → odd.
One even factor makes a product even. A product is odd only if every factor is odd.
Powers do not change parity (positive whole exponents).
Division: plug in three times, with numbers close together.
A plug-in can disprove "always", but it cannot prove it.

steps.stem: x and y are positive integers, and \(x+y\) is odd. Which of the following is true about the expression \(x^y+y^x+7+6x\)?
choices: It is odd when \(x\) is odd and \(y\) is even.
It is odd when \(x\) is even and \(y\) is odd.
explanation: Powers do not change parity, so delete them: the expression has the same parity as \(x+y+7+6x\).
\(x+y\) is odd (given), \(7\) is odd, and \(6x\) is even. Odd + odd + even = even.
So the expression is always even. Check: \(x=1\), \(y=2\): \(1^2+2^1+7+6=16\). \(x=2\), \(y=1\): \(2^1+1^2+7+12=22\). Both are even.

steps.stem: x and y are integers. x is even and not \(0\), and y is odd. Which of the following is the most precise description of \(\frac{4y}{x^3}\)?
explanation: x is even, so \(x=2k\) (\(k\) is an integer, \(k\ne0\)). Then \(x^3=8k^3\).
The top, \(y\), is odd. The bottom, \(2k^3\), is even. Odd divided by even is never an integer, so the result is always a fraction.

steps.stem: x and y are integers. Given: \(x-y=4\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: \(x-y=4\) is even, so x and y have the same parity: both even or both odd.
Why (4) is always even: \(x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y)=4(x+y)\).

steps.title: Special products
steps.intro: These products are ALWAYS divisible by a number, and each rule has a reason. For any other product, the smallest case gives only a candidate.

tables.title: Proven rules
head: Product of…
Why
Always divisible by
rows: one is even, one is divisible by 3
one is divisible by 4, another is even, one is divisible by 3
one of them is divisible by 4

tables.title: The smallest case is only a candidate
head: Product of…
Smallest case
Second case
Always divisible by

tips: Smallest case → cross out the choices that do not divide it. Then test a second case that avoids the factor you are checking.
Integer? Count the twos. \(m\) even, \(n\) odd: \(\frac{m^2(n+1)}{8}\) has three twos on top, so it is always an integer.
Never use a case that gives 0: 0 is divisible by every number, so it tells you nothing.

steps.stem: x is an odd number. Which of the following is the most precise description of \(\frac{x^2-1}{2}\)?
explanation: \(x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)\). x is odd, so \(x-1\) and \(x+1\) are two consecutive even numbers. One of them is divisible by 4, so the product is divisible by 8: \(x^2-1=8k\).
\(\frac{8k}{2}=4k\), which is always even.

steps.stem: x is an integer. The expression \(\frac{x^3-x}{3}\) is always —
explanation: \(x^3-x=x(x^2-1)=(x-1)\cdot x\cdot(x+1)\): three consecutive integers. Their product is divisible by 6: \(x^3-x=6k\).
\(\frac{6k}{3}=2k\), which is always even.
Check: \(x=1, 2, 3\) give \(0\), \(2\), \(8\). \(x=2\) gives \(2\), which is not divisible by 4, so (3) is out.

steps.stem: n is a positive odd number. The product \(n(n+2)(n+4)\) is necessarily divisible by —
explanation: Smallest case: \(n=1\) gives \(1\cdot3\cdot5=15\). A number that always divides the product must divide \(15\). \(45\) does not, so (1) is out.
The smallest case is only a candidate. Test a second case with no multiple of 5: \(n=7\) gives \(7\cdot9\cdot11=693\). It ends in 3, so it is not divisible by 5, and not by 15. (2) and (3) are out.
Why 3 always works: every third odd number is a multiple of 3 (\(3, 9, 15, 21, \dots\)). Three odd numbers in a row always include one of them.
Trap: \(n=3\) gives \(105\) and \(n=5\) gives \(315\). Both are divisible by 15, because each product has a 5 inside.

steps.stem: Given: \(p<q<0<r<s\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily negative?
explanation: Bigger minus smaller is positive, and smaller minus bigger is negative. So \(q-p>0\), \(s-r>0\), \(r-s<0\) and \(p-q<0\). Also \(p<0\) and \(-r<0\).
Only (4) is necessarily negative. Check with \(p=-2\), \(q=-1\), \(r=1\), \(s=2\): (4) gives \(1\cdot(-1)=-1\).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a<b \\ ab<0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?
explanation: \(ab<0\): a and b have opposite signs. Since \(a<b\), the negative one is a: \(a<0<b\).
(1) The top, \(b^2-a\), is positive plus positive, so it is positive. The bottom, \(a\), is negative. Positive divided by negative: negative.
(2) \(\frac{a^2-b^2}{a-b}=\frac{(a-b)(a+b)}{a-b}=a+b\). Mixed signs: the sign depends on which number is bigger in size. Not necessarily positive.
(3) The top, \(a-b\), is smaller minus bigger: negative. The bottom, \(a\), is negative. Negative divided by negative: always positive.
(4) \(\frac{ab^2}{ba^2}=\frac ba\), which is positive divided by negative, so it is negative.
Check with \(a=-1\), \(b=1\): the four choices give \(-2\), \(0\), \(2\), \(-1\). Only (3) is positive.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} d<e \\ d+e+f>0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following additional givens makes f necessarily positive?
explanation: (2) If \(e<0\), then \(d<e<0\). Both are negative, so \(d+e<0\). For \(d+e+f\) to be positive, f must be positive.
The other choices do not force f to be positive:

steps.stem:
m and n are consecutive even numbers, and p and q are consecutive even numbers. Given:
\(\begin{cases} m<n \\ p<q \\ p+n\ne0 \end{cases}\)
\(\frac{n^2-m^2+q^2-p^2}{p+n}=?\)
explanation: Consecutive even numbers: \(n=m+2\) and \(q=p+2\).
The top: \(4m+4p+8=4(m+p+2)\). The bottom: \(p+n=p+m+2\).

steps.stem: a, b and c are consecutive integers, and \(a<b<c\). Given: \(a^2+b^2=c^2\). Which of the following could be the sum of a, b and c?
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(a=b-1\), \(c=b+1\).
\(b=4\): the numbers are \(3, 4, 5\), with sum \(12\). \(b=0\): the numbers are \(-1, 0, 1\), with sum \(0\).
Only \(12\) is among the choices. Check: \(9+16=25\) ✓.
Faster: sum = count × middle, so the middle is the sum divided by 3. For \(12\) the middle is \(4\): \(3^2+4^2=5^2\) ✓.

steps.stem: a and x are integers. Given: \(x=(a-6)^2+(a+5)^3\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: \(a-6\) has the same parity as a (subtracting an even number). \(a+5\) has the opposite parity (adding an odd number).
Powers do not change parity, so \(x\) has the same parity as \((a-6)+(a+5)=2a-1\), which is always odd.
So x is always odd, and a can be even or odd. Check: \(a=1\) gives \(25+216=241\). \(a=2\) gives \(16+343=359\). Both odd.

steps.stem: m, p, q and r are integers. Given: \(2m+1=(p+1)^2\cdot q^5\cdot(r-1)^2\). Which of the numbers m, p, q, r is necessarily odd?
explanation: \(2m+1\) is odd for every integer m. So the product on the right is odd.
A product is odd only if every factor is odd.
\((p+1)^2\) is odd, so \(p+1\) is odd and p is even. \(q^5\) is odd, so q is odd. \((r-1)^2\) is odd, so \(r-1\) is odd and r is even.

steps.stem: m is an even positive number, and n is an odd positive number. Which of the following expressions is not necessarily an integer?
explanation: Count the twos. m is even, so it has at least one two. n is odd, so \(n+1\) and \(n-1\) are even.
(1) In \(m(n+1)^2\) there is one two from m and two twos from \((n+1)^2\). Three twos, enough for \(8=2^3\). Always an integer.
(2) In \(m^2n^2\) there are only two twos for sure (n is odd). With \(m=2\) and \(n=1\) the value is \(\frac{4\cdot1}{8}=\frac12\). Not necessarily an integer.
(3) \((m+n)^2-(m-n)^2=4mn\). With \(m=2k\): \(8kn\). Always divisible by 8.
(4) \(n-1\) and \(n+1\) are consecutive even numbers, so their product is divisible by 8.
The answer is (2).

steps.stem: n is an integer. Which of the following expressions is necessarily odd?
explanation: \(2n^2\) is even, so \(2n^2+1\) is always odd.
The others fail: (1) \(n(n+1)\) is a product of consecutive numbers, always even. (3) \(n=1\): \(1+1=2\), even. (4) \(2n\) is always even.

steps.stem: a and b are odd integers. Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: Why (4) is always even: odd + odd = even.

steps.stem: a and b are integers, and \(ab\) is odd. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: a and b are both positive
exactly one of a and b is even
a and b are both odd
explanation: One even factor makes a product even. The product is odd, so neither factor is even: both are odd.
The others fail: \(a=-1\), \(b=3\) gives an odd product, but a is not positive, and \(a+b=2\) is even.

steps.stem: In class A, every child has 4 pencils. In class D, every child has 5 pencils. The number of children in class D is odd. The total number of pencils of all the children in classes A and D is necessarily —
explanation: Total \(=4\cdot(\text{children in A})+5\cdot(\text{children in D})\).
\(4\) times any number is even. \(5\) times an odd number is odd × odd = odd.
Even + odd = odd, so the total is necessarily odd.
Check: 1 child in A and 1 child in D: \(4+5=9\). Odd, and not divisible by 4 or by 5.

steps.stem: The number \(10^7+7^{10}\) is —
explanation: \(10^7\) is even. \(7^{10}\) is odd (an odd number to any power is odd). Even + odd = odd.
An odd number is not divisible by 10. It is not divisible by 7 either: \(7^{10}\) is divisible by 7, but \(10^7\) is not, so the sum is not.

steps.stem: The sum of three consecutive integers is \(48\). What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = count × middle, so the middle number is \(\frac{48}{3}=16\).
The numbers are \(15, 16, 17\). The largest is \(17\).

steps.stem: How many even integers are there between \(-7\) and \(9\)?
explanation: List them: \(-6, -4, -2, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8\). That is 8 numbers. Remember: \(0\) is even.
Or count the steps of two from \(-6\) to \(8\): \(\frac{8-(-6)}{2}+1=7+1=8\).

steps.stem: Given: \(a<b<0<c\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily negative?
explanation: (3) a and b are both negative. Negative + negative = negative, always.
The others: (1) Mixed signs: the sign depends on which number is bigger in size. \(a=-2\), \(c=5\) gives \(3>0\). (2) Bigger minus smaller: positive. (4) Negative × negative: positive.

steps.stem: Given: \(x<y<0\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?
explanation: (3) Bigger minus smaller is positive, even when both numbers are negative: \(y-x>0\).
The others: (1) Negative + negative: negative. (2) Smaller minus bigger: negative. (4) Not fixed: \(x=-3\), \(y=-2\) gives \(-3+4=1\), but \(x=-10\), \(y=-1\) gives \(-10+1=-9\).

steps.stem: Given: \(p^5\cdot q^4<0\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: \(q^4\) is an even power, so \(q^4\ge0\). If \(q=0\), the product is \(0\), which is not negative. So \(q\ne0\) and \(q^4>0\).
Then \(p^5\) must be negative. An odd power keeps the sign, so \(p<0\).
The sign of q is not known: \(p=-1\), \(q=1\) and \(p=-1\), \(q=-1\) both work.

steps.stem: The sum of four consecutive even integers is \(44\). What is the smallest of them?
explanation: Write them as \(n, n+2, n+4, n+6\). The sum is \(4n+12=44\), so \(4n=32\) and \(n=8\).
Or count × middle: the middle is \(\frac{44}{4}=11\), halfway between \(10\) and \(12\). The numbers are \(8, 10, 12, 14\).

steps.stem: The sum of five consecutive integers is \(85\). What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = count × middle, so the middle number is \(\frac{85}{5}=17\).
The numbers are \(15, 16, 17, 18, 19\). The largest is \(19\).

steps.stem: How many integers are there from \(-5\) to \(20\) (inclusive)?
explanation: From a to b (inclusive) there are \(b-a+1\) integers.
Check the rule on a small case: from \(1\) to \(3\) there are 3 numbers, and \(3-1+1=3\).

steps.stem: What is the sum of all the integers from \(-12\) to \(15\) (inclusive)?
explanation: Each number from \(-12\) to \(-1\) cancels its opposite from \(1\) to \(12\). Zero adds nothing.
Check with count × middle: there are \(15-(-12)+1=28\) numbers, and the middle is \(\frac{-12+15}{2}=1.5\). \(28\cdot1.5=42\) ✓.

steps.stem: m and n are odd numbers. Which of the following expressions cannot be an integer?
explanation: m and n are odd, so \(mn\) is odd, and \(m\cdot\frac n2=\frac{mn}{2}\) is an odd number divided by 2. Never an integer.

steps.stem: x and y are integers. Given: \(x-y=6\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: \(x-y=6\) is even, so x and y have the same parity.
\(x+y\): even + even or odd + odd. Always even.
\(x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y)=6(x+y)\). Always even.
\(x^2+y^2\): powers do not change parity, so it has the parity of \(x+y\). Always even.
All three are always even. Check with \(x=7\), \(y=1\): \(8\), \(48\), \(50\).

steps.stem:
a and b are positive consecutive integers, and \(a<b\). Given: \(a^2-b^2=-9\)
\(a+b=?\)
explanation: Consecutive: \(b-a=1\), so \(a-b=-1\) and \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)=-(a+b)\).
Shortcut: for consecutive \(a<b\), \(b^2-a^2=a+b\). Check: \(a=4\), \(b=5\): \(16-25=-9\) ✓.

steps.stem:
a, b and c are consecutive positive integers, and \(a<b<c\). Given: \(c^2-a^2=48\)
\(b=?\)
explanation: Consecutive: \(b=a+1\) and \(c=a+2\), so \(c-a=2\) and \(c+a=2a+2\).

steps.stem: Given: \(x<y<z<0\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?
explanation: All three numbers are negative.
(1) \(xy>0\), divided by \(z<0\): negative.
(2) \(x+y<0\) (negative + negative) and \(-z>0\): negative.
(3) \((-x)(-y)>0\), times \(z<0\): negative.
(4) \(x<0\) and \(y+z<0\) (negative + negative). Negative × negative = positive, always. The answer is (4).

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a+b<0 \\ ab>0 \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: \(a<0\), but the sign of \(b\) cannot be determined
explanation: \(ab>0\): a and b have the same sign, and neither of them is \(0\).
If both were positive, the sum would be positive. The sum is negative, so both are negative.

steps.stem: How many odd integers are there from \(11\) to \(59\) (inclusive)?
explanation: Odd numbers go up in steps of 2. The number of steps from 11 to 59 is \(\frac{59-11}{2}=24\).
Add 1 for the first number: \(24+1=25\).
Check the rule on a small case: from \(1\) to \(5\) the odd numbers are \(1, 3, 5\), and \(\frac{5-1}{2}+1=3\) ✓.

steps.stem:
a, b and c are consecutive integers, and \(a<b<c\). Given: \(a^2+c^2=12b-16\)
\(a+b+c=?\)
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(a=b-1\), \(c=b+1\).
The numbers are \(2, 3, 4\), and the sum is \(3b=9\). Check: \(4+16=20\) and \(12\cdot3-16=20\) ✓.

steps.stem:
a, b and c are consecutive integers, and \(0<a<b<c\). The product of the three numbers is 8 times their sum.
\(b=?\)
explanation: Write the numbers around the middle: \(a=b-1\), \(c=b+1\). The sum is \(3b\) (count × middle). The product is \((b-1)b(b+1)\).

steps.stem: p and q are prime numbers, and \(p\le q\). Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
explanation: If \(q=2\), then \(p\le2\) forces \(p=2\): \(p(q+1)=2\cdot3=6\), even.
If q is an odd prime, \(q+1\) is even, so \(p(q+1)\) is even.

steps.stem: n is an even number. Which of the following could be the value of \(\frac{n^3}{2}\)?
explanation: n is even: \(n=2k\). Then \(n^3=8k^3\), so \(\frac{n^3}{2}=4k^3\). It must be divisible by 4.

steps.stem: j and n are integers. Given: \(2n+1=j(4j+1)\). j is necessarily —
explanation: \(2n+1\) is odd for every integer n. \(4j+1\) is also odd, because \(4j\) is even.
A product is odd only if every factor is odd. So j is odd.
Divisibility by 3 is not fixed: \(j=1\) gives \(1\cdot5=5=2\cdot2+1\) (\(n=2\)), and \(j=3\) gives \(3\cdot13=39=2\cdot19+1\) (\(n=19\)).

steps.stem: a and b are consecutive integers. Given: \(x=a^2-b^2+3a-3b\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation: a and b are consecutive: \(a-b=1\) or \(a-b=-1\). Also \(a+b\) is odd (one even, one odd), so \(a+b+3\) is odd + odd = even.
So \(x=(\pm1)\cdot(\text{even})\), and x is always even.
The sign is not fixed: \(a=2\), \(b=1\) gives \(x=1\cdot6=6\). \(a=1\), \(b=2\) gives \(x=(-1)\cdot6=-6\).

steps.stem: m and n are integers. The expression \((m+1)(4n+m)\) is necessarily —
explanation: \(4n\) is even, so \(4n+m\) has the same parity as m. \(m+1\) has the opposite parity. So one of the two factors is even, and the product is always even.

The others fail: (1) With \(m=-3\) and \(n=1\) the product is \((-2)\cdot1=-2\), negative. (3) With \(m=-1\) the product is \(0\). (4) With \(m=3\) and \(n=1\) the product is \(4\cdot7=28\), not divisible by 3.

steps.stem: Which of the following could be the sum of four consecutive integers?
explanation: The sum of \(a, a+1, a+2, a+3\) is \(4a+6=4(a+1)+2\): even, but never divisible by 4.
\(20\), \(24\) and \(28\) are divisible by 4, so they are out.

steps.stem: The sum of ten consecutive integers is \(5\). What is the largest of them?
explanation: Sum = count × middle, so the middle is \(\frac{5}{10}=0.5\). With an even count, the middle is halfway between the two middle numbers: \(0\) and \(1\).
Five numbers from \(1\) up: \(1, 2, 3, 4, 5\). Five numbers from \(0\) down: \(0, -1, -2, -3, -4\).
The largest is \(5\). Check: \(-4\) to \(4\) cancel out, and \(5\) is left ✓.

steps.stem: n is a positive integer. The product \((n+1)(n+2)(n+3)\) is necessarily divisible by —
explanation: Three consecutive integers: the product is always divisible by 6 (one of them is even, and one is divisible by 3).
The smallest case, \(n=1\), gives \(2\cdot3\cdot4=24\). All four choices divide 24, so it only gives candidates.
Second case: \(n=2\) gives \(3\cdot4\cdot5=60\). \(24\) and \(8\) do not divide 60. Out.
A case with no multiple of 4: \(n=4\) gives \(5\cdot6\cdot7=210\). \(12\) does not divide 210. Out. The answer is \(6\).

steps.stem: n is an odd number. \(n^2-1\) is necessarily divisible by —
explanation: \(n^2-1=(n-1)(n+1)\): two consecutive even numbers. One is divisible by 4 and the other by 2, so the product is divisible by 8.
Do not use \(n=1\): it gives \(0\), and \(0\) is divisible by every number. It tells you nothing.
\(n=5\) gives \(24\): \(16\) and \(48\) are out. \(n=3\) gives \(8\): \(24\) is out. The answer is \(8\).

steps.stem: k is an integer. Which of the following expressions is necessarily an integer?
explanation: (2) Four consecutive integers: the product is always divisible by 24, so it is divisible by 8. Always an integer.

steps.stem:
m and n are positive integers, and \(n<m\). Given:
\(\begin{cases} m^2n\text{ is even} \\ m+n\text{ is odd} \end{cases}\)
Which of the following statements is not correct?
explanation: \(m+n\) is odd, so one of m and n is even and the other is odd.
\(mn^2\) contains the even one, so it is even. The statement "\(mn^2\) is odd" is not correct.
The others are correct: (1) \(m^2+m=m(m+1)\) is a product of consecutive numbers, so it is even. (2) \(m+n+1=\text{odd}+1=\text{even}\). (4) Even minus odd, or odd minus even, is odd.

steps.stem: n is an integer greater than 1. At least half of the integers from 1 to n (inclusive) are —
explanation: The list starts with 1, which is odd, and then goes odd, even, odd, even. So there are never fewer odd numbers than even numbers.
For \(n=4\), \(1\) and \(3\) are odd (2 of 4, exactly half). For \(n=5\), \(1\), \(3\) and \(5\) are odd (3 of 5, more than half).
The others fail: (2) For \(n=3\), only \(2\) is even (1 of 3). (3) For \(n=9\), the primes are \(2, 3, 5, 7\) (4 of 9, less than half). (4) For \(n=3\), only \(1\) is not prime (1 of 3).

steps.stem: a and b are positive integers. Given: \(ab=36\). Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: if b is \(\text{odd}\) then a is \(\text{even}\)
if a is \(\text{even}\) then b is \(\text{odd}\)
explanation: \(36=2^2\cdot3^2\). If b is odd, b has no factor 2, so both twos are in a. Then a is even. So (3) is always true.

steps.stem:
Given:
\(\begin{cases} a<b \\ ab<c \end{cases}\)
Which of the following is not possible?
explanation: If \(b<0\), then \(a<b<0\). Both are negative, so \(ab>0\).
If also \(c<0\), then \(ab<c\) says that a positive number is less than a negative number. Impossible. So (4) is not possible.

steps.stem: m and n are positive integers. m is even and n is odd. Which of the following expressions is necessarily an integer?
explanation: Count the twos. n is odd, so \(n-1\) and \(n+1\) are consecutive even numbers: one is divisible by 2 and the other by 4. That is three twos. m is even: one more two. Four twos: \(2^4=16\). So (1) is always an integer.
